key_insight: A DSL-guided, predicate-based LLM agent can reason more reliably about inverse materials design by grounding natural-language rules in statistical evidence from materials data.
engineering_relevance: This approach offers a training-light path to generate and refine candidate perovskite oxides for target properties, reducing dependence on large task-specific datasets.
method: Translate design rules into symbolic predicates using a predefined chemistry DSL
Use predicates to query accumulated materials data and validate or reject rules during the design loop
Deploy a multi-agent framework (ORCHESTRA) to iteratively propose, test, and refine inverse-design candidates
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the DSL-guided framework improved rule validation and showed better design performance than natural-language-only guidance, especially for challenging target properties.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the underlying rule store and materials data, so sparse or biased data could limit reliability.
paper_title: Symbolic Predicate-Guided Language Agents for Inverse Design of Perovskite Oxides
